title: Imagery registration: gerizim
frame: place frame: metres from the place anchor in atlas/app/atlas-data.json, x east, z south, MapLibre Mercator scaled at the anchor (tools/build_osm_context.py Frame)
turnConvention: turnDegClockwise: the plan's page axes are turned clockwise on the map by this angle (east towards south); pxPerM: plan pixels per metre; planPoint (pixels) lands on placePoint (place frame)

imagery.service: Esri World Imagery (World_Imagery MapServer), zoom-18 tiles; metadata from its identify query at the place anchor
imagery.use: measurement only; tiles and resampled images are not archived (Esri terms of use)

method: The plan is matched to Vantor WorldView-2 imagery (Esri World Imagery, 21 October 2023, 0.5 m, stated accuracy 5 m) by searching the turn, scale and shift that put its dark pixels on the imagery's edges (tools/imagery_registration.py fit), then checked by overlay and an independent part or source.

figures.citation: Magen 2008, NEAEHL 5 p. 1743, 'Mount Gerizim: plan of the site' (0–50 m bar, north arrow)

checks.enclosureOnImagery: the Byzantine cloister enclosure measures about 71 × 57 m on the imagery and 70 × 60 m on the plan

figures.citation: Magen 2008, NEAEHL 5 p. 1746, 'Plan of the Persian and Hellenistic period sacred precinct' (0–25 m bar; north arrow points left)

checks.agreementWithSitePlan: walls of both plans coincide within 1–2 m over the precinct (overlay)
checks.westWall: core west wall 83.1 m on the registered plan; Magen 2008 p. 1746: 84 m
checks.scale: fitted 7.88 px/m is 1.5 % above the bar (7.76)

positionsNote: Read on the registered plans (precinct plan for the precinct, site plan for the mansion), about ±2 m; the summit platform stands for the reported 212 × 136 m enclosure.

placement.note: the model is built in the place frame from these positions

uncertainty_m: about 2 between plan and imagery; the imagery's own stated accuracy is 5
